Posterior-predictive check of a surrogate against held-out outputs

Source: R/surrogate_ppc.R
fb_surrogate_ppc.Rd

Tests whether a surrogate's predictive distribution matches the simulator's at held-out parameter sets, using kernR's maximum-mean-discrepancy posterior-predictive check (kernR::mmd_ppc()). The surrogate's predictive distribution at newdata is sampled into a predictive ensemble, which is compared against observed – the true simulator outputs at those parameter sets. A rejection means the emulator distorted the output distribution (typically by being over- or under-dispersed, or by getting the cross-output correlation wrong), not merely that its mean is off.

Usage

fb_surrogate_ppc(
  surrogate,
  newdata,
  observed,
  n_draws = 1L,
  joint = TRUE,
  project = FALSE,
  whiten = FALSE,
  aggregate = FALSE,
  agg_weights = "uniform",
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

surrogate

An fb_surrogate from fit_surrogate().

newdata

A data.frame of held-out parameter sets (must contain the surrogate's parameter columns).

observed

A matrix or data.frame of the true simulator outputs at held-out parameter sets, with columns named for the emulated outputs.

n_draws

Predictive draws per row of newdata (default 1); the predictive ensemble has n_draws * nrow(newdata) rows.

joint

Logical; sample from the joint cross-output covariance (default TRUE) rather than independently per output. Has no effect for a single output, or for a surrogate that reports only marginals (its covariance is diagonal). When the surrogate stores a low-rank covariance (cov_rank), the joint draws are sampled from the factored form directly, so the k x k slice is never formed (the native low-rank PPC consumer).

project

Logical; for a surrogate that stores a low-rank covariance (cov_rank), project both the predictive draws and observed onto the surrogate's q factor directions before the MMD (default FALSE). It then runs in q dimensions, not k – cheaper and higher-powered on the correlated cross-output structure for a large output count (the MMD loses power as the dimension grows). It is, deliberately, blind to distortions orthogonal to the factor space (purely idiosyncratic per-output errors, which the marginal <o>_sd and a joint = FALSE check cover), so it complements rather than replaces the full-space check.

whiten

Logical; Mahalanobis-whiten both the predictive draws and observed by their pooled covariance before the MMD (default FALSE). This puts the outputs on a common footing, removing the cross-output scale heterogeneity that makes a single median bandwidth too coarse to resolve a distortion living in a low-variance direction. The map depends only on the pooled cloud (not the draws-vs-observed labels), so the permutation test stays valid; the same map is applied to both clouds, so a relative scale, shape, or mean difference between them is preserved. Empirically it lifts power substantially on localised / heterogeneous-scale distortions a raw-output check misses, with no blind spot found across a mean / variance / shape battery. A graduated relative ridge guards a near-singular pooled covariance (highly collinear outputs); it remains opt-in for that numerical reason. Composes with project (the projected coordinates are whitened) and aggregate.

aggregate

Logical; run an aggregated multi-kernel MMD instead of a single-kernel (default FALSE). An MMDAgg test (Schrab et al. 2023) over an RBF bandwidth grid around the median heuristic, sharing the permutations across bandwidths and aggregating by the weighted-quantile statistic min_g p_g / w_g – it removes the bandwidth choice and is robust when the median heuristic is mis-scaled, at a valid level. Composes with project. Reads n_permutations and alpha from ....

agg_weights

Kernel weights for aggregate = TRUE: a scheme ("uniform" default, or "increasing" / "decreasing" / "centred", ordered smallest-to-largest bandwidth) or a numeric vector over the bandwidth grid. A larger weight loosens that kernel's threshold, so up-weighting the scale a distortion is expected to live at recovers power; "uniform" is the safe default (it recovers the min p-value aggregation).

seed

Optional integer RNG seed (the caller's stream is restored).

...

Passed to kernR::mmd_ppc() (e.g. n_permutations); for aggregate = TRUE, n_permutations and alpha are read from here.

Value

For the single-kernel, the kernR::mmd_ppc object ($statistic, $p_value, $reject, $surprise_bits); for aggregate = TRUE an fb_mmd_agg object ($p_value, $reject, $statistic, $bandwidths, $p_per_bandwidth).

Details

This is the distribution-preserving counterpart to a mean-only accuracy check: it exercises the predictive uncertainty it reports, not just the mean. With joint = TRUE (default) the draws are sampled from the full cross-output predictive covariance (predict.fb_surrogate() with cov = TRUE), so the emulator's cross-output correlation is tested; this is the second consumer of the joint covariance after fb_surrogate_ies(). With joint = FALSE each output is sampled independently from its <o>_sd. On a simulator whose outputs are correlated, marginal draws discard that correlation, so the joint path is the faithful check (a marginals-only surrogate yields a diagonal covariance, and the two paths then coincide).

See also

fit_surrogate(), predict.fb_surrogate(), fb_surrogate_ies().

Examples

g <- rbind(c(1.5, -0.8), c(0.4, 1.1))
theta <- cbind(p1 = runif(80, -2, 2), p2 = runif(80, -2, 2))
y <- theta %*% t(g) + matrix(rnorm(160, 0, 0.1), 80, 2L)
colnames(y) <- c("o1", "o2")
ens <- fb_ensemble(as.data.frame(theta), as.data.frame(y),
                    provenance = list(source = "raw"))
sur <- fit_surrogate(ens)

held <- data.frame(p1 = runif(30, -2, 2), p2 = runif(30, -2, 2))
truth_held <- held$p1 %o% g[, 1] + held$p2 %o% g[, 2] +
  matrix(rnorm(60, 0, 0.1), 30, 2L)
colnames(truth_held) <- c("o1", "o2")
check <- fb_surrogate_ppc(sur, held, as.data.frame(truth_held),
                           n_draws = 3L, seed = 1L, n_permutations = 99L)
check$p_value
#> [1] 0.94
